claim: A Home Ministry report on human trafficking dated November 2023 says that in January to September 2023 courts disposed of 332 cases under the trafficking act and all the accused were acquitted in 316 of them, 95.18% of the total.

claim: After no convictions in 2021 and 2022 the Home Ministry issued an instruction on investigating trafficking cases which says the crime takes place in six stages from going abroad to returning, and tells investigators to collect who trafficked the victim, who introduced the victim to the ring, whether the victim was threatened, abducted by force or trafficked by exploiting a vulnerability, and by what route the ring moved the victim.

claim: A 28-year-old woman from Savar who was told she would be sent to Canada was trafficked to Nadia district in West Bengal, India, and came home after seven months in a jail there, Prothom Alo reported in January 2024.
draft_quotes: কানাডায় পাঠানোর কথা বলে সাভারের একজন নারীকে (২৮) ভারতের পশ্চিমবঙ্গের নদীয়া জেলায় পাচার করা হয়। সেখানে একটি জেলে সাত মাস বন্দী থেকে দেশে ফেরেন তিনি।

claim: The Savar woman's father, who filed the trafficking case, told Prothom Alo in January 2024 that the accused then filed a false case against him at Savar police station, that he was arrested and spent four months in jail, that it cost him Tk 5 to 6 lakh, and that he had now heard all the accused in his case had been acquitted.

claim: A 34-year-old Narayanganj woman went to Saudi Arabia in July 2022 after being told she would do housework for Tk 30,000 a month, and was physically and mentally abused there; her husband said the people who had sent her demanded Tk 3 lakh 20 thousand to bring her back, and that she was put out of the house after threatening suicide and then came home.

claim: Nearly three years after the TikTok trafficking case was filed in Dhaka the investigation was not finished, although accused arrested in India over the same incident had already been tried and punished there, Prothom Alo reported in January 2024; Salma Ali of BNWLA said the lack of accountability of those investigating is why accused are not properly punished.

claim: The government keeps no count of workers who come back, except those who return on an outpass after losing their passport, whom the Wage Earners' Welfare Board's desk at the airport records; by that record 86,621 workers came back empty-handed from various countries in 2023, 2,902 of them women, including 249 women in December 2023.

claim: Officials of several government bodies told Prothom Alo in January 2024 that most women who leave a Saudi household before the two-year contract ends run away and take shelter in the embassy's safe home, from where they are sent to the Saudi government's safe home, and the Saudi government pays for sending them home; if a woman wants to return within three months of arriving, her return is arranged through the Saudi company that recruited her.

claim: Lutfa Begum said she was paid no wages for her work in Saudi Arabia in 2020, and that after coming home she received Tk 30,000 in cash assistance in two instalments.
